note: Mock content for the prototype. The ship and its history are invented.

core.text: This sea chest belonged to one of the Marigold's sailors. Everything a sailor owned for a voyage of many months had to fit inside a box this size.
The chest doubled as a seat and a table below deck. The rope handles were knotted by the sailor who owned it, and each one is a little different.
Inside the lid is a painting of the ship, made during long weeks at sea, so the owner could still see her once back home.

open_question.text: What would you pack if it all had to fit in here?

additions.text: Look closely at the painted lid: the flag on the main mast is the shipowner's own flag, so we know which ship this is.
The handles are called beckets. Sailors tied them in fancy knots in their spare time, partly for pride and partly for practice.
To go a bit deeper: a list found inside names a spare shirt, oilskins, a sewing kit, a knife, letters and a small Bible. Not much for six months.
Sailors on watch steered by the compass we saw on the other side of the room; off watch, this chest was most of their private space.

qa.text: The name painted inside is J. Harlow, an able seaman who sailed on the Marigold for six years.
It's pine, painted on the outside to keep the damp out.

qa_fallback.text: That's a good question, and I don't know the answer. What we do know is that this chest went to sea with the Marigold for six years.
